name: One&Only Moonlight Basin, Montana
positioning: All-season alpine resort in Big Sky, Montana, set on 240 acres bordered by the protected lands of the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem, with architecture by Tom Kundig
best_for: Skiers and snowsports fans who also want a full spa and cabin-style privacy
Families and outdoor lovers looking for hiking, biking, fly-fishing and wildlife in the warmer months

facts.text: The resort is set on 240 acres within a vast 8,100-acre landscape bordered by the protected lands of the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem.
In winter there are slopes for snowsports; in the warmer months, hiking, biking and fly-fishing.
The architecture and design are by architect Tom Kundig and interact with the landscape.
The resort is flanked by animal habitats, including those of endangered grizzly bears, and experiences here are expert-led.
Even the smallest rooms feature a fireplace, a private balcony and a bathroom with a soaking tub and separate shower.
The spa includes an indoor-outdoor lap pool, a heated onsen soaking tub, a cold plunge, a steam room and a sauna.
Akira Back is a restaurant led by Chef Akira Back, known for creative takes on Japanese-Korean fusion.
On-site trails are open for snowshoeing, fat tire biking and cross-country Nordic skiing.
The KidsOnly club offers outdoor programming for children.
Half of the rooms can be connected to other rooms to form a family suite.
There is a tennis court and an outdoor yoga deck just outside the spa.
Dogs are welcome, with a limit of two dogs per booking.

highlights.text: The private cabins each have an outdoor deck with a private fire pit and hot tub.
The hotel has a private observatory where a local astronomer can lead stargazing sessions on request.
Every guest, no matter their room category, is paired with an on-property host.
The spa includes an indoor-outdoor lap pool and a heated onsen soaking tub.
The resort sits on 240 acres bordered by the protected lands of the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem.

considerations.text: Big Sky is around an hour's drive from Bozeman International Airport; the resort can arrange private transfers.
All transfers are subject to weather conditions and may be delayed or rescheduled in adverse weather.
WhataHotel notes the remote mountain location requires travel planning.
